newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS - Telekom soars on earnings optimism.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Telekom soars on earnings optimism.

text.p: Shares in Deutsche Telekom AG surged to record levels on Monday as investors bet on upbeat earnings news from the newly listed German telecommunications giant, which holds its annual news conference on Tuesday.
Telekom shares led turnover through the day and hit an all-time high of 41.95 marks , a rise of 47 percent from its issue price last November of 28.50 marks a share.
The stock later eased to trade up 1.25 marks, or 3.2 percent, at 41.20 marks in bourse trade, while the blue chip DAX index notched up a modest gain of 0.15 percent.
The sale of Telekom shares last year marked Europe's biggest ever initial public offering, and attracted a lot of first time equity investors attracted by massive publicity campaigns.

"A lot was arguing for Telekom in the past few days," said a Frankfurt dealer, referring in part to an unconfirmed press report in Der Spiegel magazine this weekend that the company was planning measures to turn its cable business to profit, including a foray into commercial television.
"The stock passed a key psychological threshold at 40 marks, the news has been good and we seem to be expecting more of the same," the dealer said.

Preliminary results for Telekom have already been released, apart from group net profit figures for 1996, so that analysts are mainly focusing on its prospects for the coming years, with most expecting steady profit growth through to 1998.

Analysts predict that Telekom's dividend will rise to between 1.30 marks and 1.50 marks in 1997 after a payout of 60 pfennigs per share in 1996. Telekom itself has said it expects to double profits and dividend payments this year.

Telekom is expected to give more details on Tuesday about its cost reduction programme and its progress on reducing its debt burden, which it wants to cut to 65 billion marks ($39 billion) from 82 billion marks at the end of 1996.

Good news, analysts say, ought to preserve the company from taking a beating when the six month period during which taxes are levied on gains made from selling its stock ends on May 19 -- a deadline which could spark some profit-taking.

The stock's recent gains are already seen as reflecting a growing perception on the market that Telekom's would-be competitors in a market due for deregulation next year have been slower off the mark than had been expected, analysts say.
BHF Bank, bullish on Telekom which it expects to make strong progress on cost-cutting, is predicting earnings per share of 1.14 marks in 1996, 2.01 marks in 1997 and 2.56 marks in 1998.
"How Telekom deals with reducing debt and personnel is the most interesting aspect by far," said Martin Ziegenbalg, analyst at Dresdner Kleinwort Benson in Frankfurt.
Ziegenbalg forecasts Telekom's 1996 EPS at 74 pfennigs, rising to 2.03 marks in 1997 and 2.28 marks in 1998.

The company has already said its sales rose six percent to 63.1 billion marks in 1996 and earnings from ordinary activities surged more than 50 percent to more than six billion marks. Net profit at the parent company was 1.6 billion marks.
Despite overall optimism for Telekom, the stock is likely to shed some of its gains after May 19, once the capital gains tax charge is lifted from its stock.
Analysts at Paribas, noting Telekom's strong performance on Monday, cut their recommendation on the stock to "no action" from "buy".
"The shares are still supported by an excellent yield and the fact that most clients are underweight in the share, but it is difficult to envisage much outperformance," Paribas said.
Still analysts said it made sense for small investors, who came out in their droves last year for the Telekom share issue, to hang on to their investment.
($ = 1.668 German Marks)
